calls.body: The Senators are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Bruins are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Senators’ chance quality wins out.

calls.head: There’s no curse: Swayman vs. The Senators
calls.body: Swayman has been shaky against the Senators since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Swayman starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .863 against the Senators.

calls.head: The Bruins can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Senators’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Bruins’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Bruins more than most. The Bruins take a lot of penalties and the Senators draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.head: Who drives the play: the Senators
calls.body: The Senators have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Bruins around the middle. Expect the Senators to spend more of the night in the Bruins’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

BOS.head: We gave Boston only a 35% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 65% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Boston found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Boston usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Ottawa usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Boston’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Stützle has two goals and an assist as the Senators beat the Bruins
paras: Tim Stützle struck first for the Senators shorthanded early in the first, and he scored again less than two minutes later to make it 2-0. Drake Batherson and Michael Amadio scored a little over four minutes apart early in the second to stretch the lead to 4-0. Samuel Ersson took over from Linus Ullmark in net for Ottawa to start the third. James Hagens got the Bruins on the board early in the third. Stützle added an assist for a three-point night.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Jeremy Swayman stopped 20 of 24 for the Bruins.

Three players picked up ten-minute misconducts. Neither power play scored: the Senators killed all four Bruins power plays, and the Bruins killed all four of Ottawa’s. The Bruins killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes late in the first. The Senators moved to 2-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Bruins dropped to 2-2-0, losing first place in the Atlantic to the Senators.

items.text: Tim Stützle passed Wade Redden for sixth on the Senators’ all-time scoring list, with 413 points.

The Senators won without Artem Zub, Jake Sanderson and André Burakovsky. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Ducks and the Islanders were missing more at the time.
None of the preview’s four calls held.
